messages:
michael: quick follow-up from the postmortem — we still have 6 open action items. need explicit owners, jira links, and short acceptance criteria so nothing stalls.
rachel: agreed. i skimmed the doc and flagged 3 that look like recurring patterns. recommend we create an epic to group them.
diego: i'll take the infrastructure-facing item about the autoscaler config drift. created ticket RMD-9101. R: diego, A: rachel, C: eng-sre, I: support. ETA: Wed EOD.
sam: i'll own the model-proxy memory leak investigation (RMD-9102). plan: reproduce, add telemetry, propose a patch, and run canary. R: sam, A: michael, C: runtime, I: product. ETA: next Fri.
michael: thanks. for recurring-pattern tracking, can we centralize all related tickets in one epic and attach a short 2-line mitigation plan per ticket? avoids scatter.
rachel: creating EPIC-9120 "recurring-remediation-tracker" and linking RMD-9101/9102. please add any historical incidents as ticket links.
diego: added rollback steps to RMD-9101 and a one-liner rollback command for oncall. labeled `remediation:high`.
pm-bot: RMD-9101 assigned to diego; reminder set for 2026-04-09T17:00:00Z.
sam: small process ask  can we standardize R/A (single owner + single approver) and require a 1-line acceptance criteria field in Jira for quick closure? last time multiple approvers blocked closure.
michael: yes please. update RACI doc to reflect single R/A per action and a mandatory acceptance criteria field. who can volunteer to update the doc?
rachel: i can draft a short PR with suggested wording and examples (P1: 72h remediation SLA, P2: 2 weeks). will ping for review.
diego: also recommend a short 'handback' clause: if R is on leave, assign interim R with a 48h handover window. reduces orphaned tickets.
sam: noted. for RMD-9102 i'll add acceptance criteria: reproduce bug in staging, telemetry added, PR with tests, canary pass for 24h.
michael: good. let's set a quick sync next Tue 09:30 UTC to confirm status and unblock anything stuck.
rachel: added the sync to calendar and linked the epic. also creating a small dashboard to surface repeating error signatures (WIP): https://grafana.internal/d/remediations (do not share externally).
diego: question  should recurring issues live in the runbook or in the epic? i prefer epic + dashboard so remediation status is trackable over sprints.
michael: epic + dashboard sounds right. runbook can reference the epic for deeper investigation notes.
pm-bot: Follow-up sync created for 2026-04-07T09:30:00Z.
sam: i'll post investigation notes and a small smoke-test script in RMD-9102 by EOD Thu.
rachel: i'll open the RACI doc PR and add an audit field to Jira (who closed, timestamp). helps for compliance.
michael: thanks everyone. marking this thread as follow-up-in-progress. reconvene Tue 09:30. :thumbsup:
